_comment: The script is a PARAMETER of the recipe, not a fixture inside it. One file per brand. The recipe does not know or care what the arc is. Rewritten 2026-10-01 after the first real render: the previous draft declared story_with_corroborators and then wrote strict A/B/A/B for all fourteen lines with a fifty-fifty word split. That ping-pong reads as setup-and-payoff, which is the doubter-and-convert rhythm even when nobody doubts anything, and that is exactly what a viewer said it felt like. The arc was declared and not written.
_arc_note: dod-blender, the reference this arc is drawn from: ONE host tells a true story and the other interjects, confirms, adds a detail. So host A carries it in runs of two and three lines, host B lands five short ones, and the word split is about seventy-thirty. The product is named at line four, which is a quarter of the way in; the reference names it at thirty-eight percent. It ends on a half-finished thought with no resolution and no call to action, which is what the reference does.

lines.text: Sunday night, fridge open, and nothing decided.
So we gave the planner a week. One week.
Monday Fernwick picked the meals and built the list.
I shopped once. Twenty minutes, in and out.
You texted me from the car park.
Tuesday was the test. Late, tired, no ideas.
And the app already had one waiting.
One pan. Nobody argued about dinner.
Nobody argues about dinner in your house.
By Friday the list was shorter. Less food binned.
That is the whole thing, really.
